reason: This passage from Ezra 3 narrates the return of the Judean exiles and the rebuilding of the Second Temple altar and foundation. It describes religious ceremonies, offerings, the appointment of Levites, and the people's emotional reactions—both weeping (from elders remembering the first temple) and joyful celebration. The text contains no discussion of complaints to leaders, nor does it present any moral teaching regarding whether people should or should not complain to their leaders. The passage focuses on restoration, faithfulness to Torah, and collective religious observance rather than on leader-follower dynamics or complaints.
